title: HubTown migration manifest
evidence_level: source-proven only; nothing here is Studio or runtime evidence

coverage.coverage_rule: Every recovered row whose path is 'Workspace/HubTown' or starts with 'Workspace/HubTown/' must be claimed by exactly one entry in this manifest. Enforced by scripts/validate_migration_manifests.py.
coverage.path_is_not_a_key: Ten HubTown names are shared by more than one instance (Crenellation, WallTorch, PlazaCrystal_1..4, CrystalPedestal_1..4). Legacy instance ids are the only unique legacy handle, so canonical content must mint its own stable ids rather than deriving them from instance names.

dispositions.KEEP: Legacy representation is already correct for the canonical architecture and can be adopted as-is.
dispositions.MIGRATE: Legacy content carries authored value and should be reconstructed as source-managed canonical content under a canonical owner.
dispositions.REPLACE: Legacy representation overlaps an existing canonical owner. Reproduce the intent through that owner; do not re-create the legacy instances or scripts as a second path.
dispositions.ARCHIVE: Preserve for reference only. Never boot, require, or map into the active project.

extraction_status_values.recovered: The row is present in the recovered workspace index and its identity is proven.
extraction_status_values.requires_studio_extraction: Identity is proven but the contents below it were lost with the damaged archive and must be re-extracted from the source place.

entries.summary: Authored hub/social space root folder.
entries.canonical_representation: A source-managed HubTown composition specification plus a reviewable placement representation. HubTown has no canonical owner in src today; BA-010 defines the composition and BA-011 the model/placement strategy.
entries.runtime_gate: integration; must not be bootstrapped before the v2.7 rollout gates and the integration gate open
entries.notes: The canonical world today is the forest/extraction setting described by WorldFoundationConfig. HubTown is a second, medieval-themed space from the legacy RPG. Reconciling those two art directions is a design decision that BA-010 must record, not an automatic port.

entries.summary: Main plaza floor slab; the hub's traversal surface and spawn reference.
entries.canonical_representation: Authored-world constant plus placement data, following the WorldFoundationConfig pattern of stable ids with replaceable graybox geometry.
entries.notes: Safe-zone boundary semantics belong to BA-010, not to the geometry itself.

entries.summary: Plaza ring border that reads the hub's circular layout.
entries.canonical_representation: Placement data under the HubTown composition specification.

entries.summary: Central emblem decal/part marking the plaza focal point.
entries.canonical_representation: A declared visual asset entry rather than an ad-hoc authored part, so the asset manifest owns its identity.
entries.notes: Do not invent an asset id. The emblem texture, if any, must be re-extracted from the place before it can be declared.

entries.summary: Emissive inner ring used as ambient plaza glow.
entries.canonical_representation: A gameplay-light descriptor validated by GameplayLightDescriptorValidator, not a free-standing emissive part.
entries.notes: Lighting already has a canonical owner. Re-creating legacy emissive parts would create a second lighting path, which the build-ahead rules forbid.

entries.summary: Four town wall segments enclosing the hub.
entries.canonical_representation: Placement data with stable per-segment ids. These segments imply the safe-zone boundary that BA-010 must state explicitly.
entries.notes: Wall segments are the only recovered evidence of the hub's extent. Their CFrames were lost, so the extent itself is unknown until re-extraction.

entries.summary: Twenty crenellation caps decorating the wall line.
entries.canonical_representation: Generated decoration derived from the wall placement rule rather than twenty hand-placed instances.
entries.notes: All twenty share the name 'Crenellation'. Decorative repetition like this should be produced by a deterministic placement rule so it costs one canonical id, not twenty.

entries.summary: Hub entry archway model.
entries.canonical_representation: A named entry landmark in the HubTown composition specification, with the model represented per BA-011.
entries.notes: The model's children were lost with the damaged archive. Re-extract before committing any representation.

entries.summary: Grand staircase model connecting plaza levels.
entries.canonical_representation: A navigation landmark in the HubTown composition specification with a reviewable model representation.
entries.notes: Traversal geometry affects character movement and cannot be validated outside Studio.

entries.summary: Central fountain model; the hub's primary visual anchor.
entries.canonical_representation: A named navigation landmark plus a reviewable model representation. Any water/particle effect it contains becomes a declared visual asset, not an inline authored effect.
entries.notes: Recovered class counts show 31 ParticleEmitter and 22 Fire instances place-wide; some are expected here, but their exact placement was lost.

entries.summary: Town banner assembly (pole, banner, tip).
entries.canonical_representation: One declared decorative asset composed of three parts, carrying a single canonical id.

entries.summary: Hanging banners identifying the apothecary, armor smith and weapon smith.
entries.canonical_representation: Wayfinding presentation bound to the vendor interaction id, so signage and vendor identity cannot drift apart.
entries.notes: These three banner names are the strongest surviving evidence that apothecary, armor_smith and weapon_smith were player-facing vendors rather than scenery. There is no HangingBanner for 'merchant' or 'quest_board'.

entries.summary: Six standing plaza torches.
entries.canonical_representation: Six gameplay-light descriptors with stable light ids, activated through the existing lighting owner.
entries.notes: Each torch id is followed by two unrecovered child ids (a PointLight and a Fire, by the gap pattern 211/214/217/...), so the emitters themselves must be re-extracted. Reproduce the lighting intent through the canonical descriptors; do not restore raw PointLight/Fire instances.

entries.summary: Eight wall-mounted torches along the town wall.
entries.canonical_representation: Gameplay-light descriptors placed by the same rule that places the wall segments.
entries.notes: All eight share the name 'WallTorch'; canonical ids must be minted, not derived. The same three-id stride suggests each carries an unrecovered PointLight and Fire.

entries.summary: Six floating magic orbs providing ambient plaza VFX.
entries.canonical_representation: Declared ambient visual assets plus gameplay-light descriptors where they actually light the space.
entries.notes: Reduced-motion and low-graphics behaviour is a canonical accessibility concern; a straight port of animated legacy orbs would bypass PresentationAccessibilityConfig.

entries.summary: Four plaza crystals, each present as two instances.
entries.canonical_representation: Declared visual assets paired with gameplay-light descriptors, mounted on the canonical pedestals.
entries.notes: Each of the four names appears twice (ids 325/337, 328/340, 331/343, 334/346). Whether that is a duplicate pair per pedestal or an authoring mistake cannot be decided without CFrames, so it is an explicit open question for re-extraction.

entries.summary: Four crystal pedestals, each present as two instances.
entries.canonical_representation: Placement data with four stable pedestal ids and an explicit mount point for the paired crystal.
entries.notes: Pedestal ids interleave with the crystal ids (325/327, 328/330, ...), which supports reading each crystal/pedestal as one authored unit.

entries.summary: Ground fog volume dressing the plaza.
entries.canonical_representation: Atmosphere expressed through the canonical lighting/fog constants, not a bespoke fog part.
entries.notes: WorldFoundationConfig.Lighting already owns FogStart/FogEnd for the canonical world. A hub-local fog part would compete with it.

entries.summary: Dungeon portal folder; the hub's expedition entry point.
entries.canonical_representation: A portal definition carrying a stable portal id, destination route/dungeon id, eligibility prerequisites and explicit denial reasons (BA-031), whose accepted launch is handed to the existing server-authoritative expedition lobby.
entries.runtime_gate: integration; launch authority stays with ExpeditionLobbyService and must not be duplicated
entries.notes: This is the single highest-value HubTown row: it is the seam between the hub and the canonical expedition loop. The place contains exactly one ProximityPrompt, which is a strong candidate for this portal's interaction, but its parent was lost. Client interaction may only request a launch; eligibility and launch remain server-owned.

entries.summary: Weapon smith vendor structure/anchor folder.
entries.canonical_representation: A vendor definition with a stable vendor id and catalog reference (BA-024) plus an interaction anchor in the HubTown interaction registry (BA-012).
entries.runtime_gate: integration; no purchase mutation path may be wired before the integration gate
entries.notes: The legacy vendor id was the folder name 'weapon_smith', which HubTownService used to key HubTownConfig.VendorCatalog. That config was never present in the place, so the catalog contents are unknown.

entries.summary: Armor smith vendor structure/anchor folder.
entries.canonical_representation: A vendor definition with a stable vendor id and catalog reference plus an interaction anchor.

entries.summary: Apothecary vendor structure/anchor folder.
entries.canonical_representation: A vendor definition with a stable vendor id and catalog reference plus an interaction anchor.
entries.notes: Consumable pricing must reference canonical inventory items rather than reviving the legacy item model.

entries.summary: General merchant structure/anchor folder.
entries.canonical_representation: A vendor definition with a stable vendor id and catalog reference plus an interaction anchor.
entries.notes: Unlike the other three vendors this one has no HangingBanner, and its instance id (367) sits far from the 125/145/165 cluster, so it was probably added later. Treat its vendor role as unconfirmed until re-extraction.

entries.summary: Quest board structure/anchor folder.
entries.canonical_representation: A quest-offer interaction anchor referencing canonical quest ids (BA-020) through the HubTown interaction registry (BA-012).
entries.runtime_gate: integration; quest state stays server-authoritative and unwired until the integration gate
entries.notes: The place holds 2 SurfaceGui and 10 TextLabel instances; some are likely the quest board's face, but their parents were lost.

entries.summary: Legacy server-authoritative hub service: vendor stock rotation, purchases and NPC interaction.
entries.canonical_representation: Vendor behaviour re-expressed as a deterministic, testable resolver over canonical inventory/currency authority. The legacy module must never be booted.
entries.runtime_gate: integration; blocked additionally by the legacy-service resurrection guard (BA-071)
entries.notes: Byte-exact source was lost with the damaged archive; a normalized readable copy survives at imports/studio-2026-08-07/readable-reference/ServerScriptService/Services/HubTownService.luau. It requires HubTownConfig and HubTownContracts, neither of which existed in the place, so it could not have run there either. Concepts worth keeping: 600s rotating stock, 60-100% catalog subset, 20% daily deal at 15-40% off, 5% rarity upgrade with a 1.3x stat bump, 15% bonus affix on purchase. Its os.clock() timing, unbounded purchase handler and client-trusted payload shape are not acceptable under canonical rules.

open_gaps.summary: No depth-3 HubTown row survives, so every folder and model listed above is an identity without contents.
open_gaps.resolution: Re-extract the Workspace hierarchy from the source place per docs/production/RBXL-IMPORT-INTEGRITY-2026-08-07.md.

open_gaps.summary: The preservation index records identity and parentage only. No CFrame, size, material, colour or attribute survived for any HubTown instance.
open_gaps.resolution: Re-extract with properties, or re-author the hub as canonical graybox and treat the legacy layout as reference only.

open_gaps.summary: HubTownConfig and HubTownContracts are named by HubTownService but were absent from the place, so the legacy vendor catalog, NPC roster, greetings and rarity value table have no surviving source anywhere.
open_gaps.resolution: Treat the vendor catalog as new canonical design work. Do not reconstruct it by guessing from HubTownService call sites.

open_gaps.summary: HubTown is a medieval RPG hub while the canonical authored world in WorldFoundationConfig is a forest/extraction setting with a survival-horror presentation language.
open_gaps.resolution: BA-010 must record an explicit art-direction decision before any geometry is migrated. This is a product decision, not a migration mechanic.
